samples.summary: docs-view's new `readOnly` remount dependency (and the `store.dispose()` it requires) has no test, while the equivalent notes and slides changes each got one
samples.evidence: This diff adds `readOnly` to the effect deps in three views. `notes-view-readonly.test.tsx` and `slides-view-readonly.test.tsx` are new and pin the rebuild+dispose for notes/slides, but nothing mounts `DocsView`: `grep -l 'DocsView|docs-view' packages/frontend/**/*.test.*` returns only `yorkie-doc-store.test.ts`, `docs-context-menu.test.tsx` and `docs-table-context-menu.test.tsx`, none of which render DocsView or exercise a readOnly flip. Docs is the surface the whole change is motivated by (the docs editor's read-only wrapper is described as the visitor's actual write boundary), and the new `store.dispose()` call in the same cleanup is also unexercised. A regression that drops `readOnly` from the deps again, or that disposes the store while the editor still needs it, would ship green.

samples.summary: The share-link periodic revalidation rewrite (useEffect → useQuery with refetchInterval/retry/error handling) has no test at all
samples.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` was rewritten from a one-shot `resolveShareLink` effect to a react-query poll (`refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, `refetchOnWindowFocus`, `retry: 1`) plus a new missing-token/error branch. Grepping `packages/frontend` `*.test.*` for `shared-document` / `SharedDocumentByToken` / `resolveShareLink` finds only `shared-blob-routing.test.ts`, `user-presence.test.tsx` and `template-review-queue.test.tsx` — none render this component. Untested behaviours that matter: a downgraded role actually propagating to `readOnly`, a revoked link closing the view, and the claimed 'two attempts have to fail before eviction' (a single blip must not evict a working session). Both failure directions are user-visible (a revoked editor keeps writing, or a healthy session is thrown out).

samples.summary: The two new Cmd+Shift+V guard tests are purely negative with no positive control, so they pass vacuously if the shortcut never fires
samples.evidence: Both new tests (`…resolves during the yield is refused`, `…resolves after dispose writes nothing`) only assert that 'PLAIN' is absent from the document. Neither asserts that `readText` was ever called, and `installPendingClipboard` returns no spy handle for that. If `dispatchPastePlain` failed to reach `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` (modifier/platform gating in `handleKeyDown`, or a future refactor of the shortcut), the clipboard read never happens and both tests still pass — i.e. the `this.disposed || this.pasting` guard added at text-editor.ts:4273 would be uncovered while appearing covered. Contrast `editor-read-only.test.ts`'s disposal paste test, which pairs the negative with a 'control: the same paste lands when the editor is still alive' case, and `editor-undo-selection.test.ts`, which asserts `readText` was called.

samples.summary: `YorkieDocStore.dispose()` (new) is never tested — nothing pins that remote-change stops reaching a discarded store
samples.evidence: `dispose()` unsubscribes and clears `onRemoteChange`; the whole point is that a store replaced while the Yorkie document stays attached must stop driving the disposed editor. `grep dispose packages/frontend/tests/app/docs/yorkie-doc-store.test.ts` returns nothing, and the new frontend tests in this diff only cover the undo-floor changes. A regression (e.g. forgetting to null the subscription) leaks a callback that refreshes and publishes presence from a disposed editor, with no test failing.

samples.summary: The `requestLayoutRefresh` seam — and specifically the `dirtyBlockIds` save/restore that keeps the deferred paint incremental — has no test
samples.evidence: `textEditor.requestLayoutRefresh` restores `dirtyBlockIds` after `recomputeLayout()` (with `undefined` mapping to an empty set), and the comment says that without it every batched keystroke re-measures the WHOLE document. Grepping `packages/docs/test` for `requestLayoutRefresh`, `withUndoUnit`, `undoUnitDepth` finds only prose mentions (memory.test.ts:318, text-box-editor.test.ts:824) — no test wires or observes it. The frontend paint test only counts paints (`ctxCalls.save === 1`); it asserts nothing about layout freshness mid-unit or about incremental reuse. A regression here is a silent large perf loss on every keystroke, plus a potentially stale `getLayout()` inside a unit (the paste path branches on `blockParentMap`).

samples.summary: `revocableDocStore`'s proxy traps are only covered indirectly for writes; the invariant-preserving traps it deliberately adds are untested
samples.evidence: The new export documents specific trap behaviour: memoized bound members so identity is stable (`s.canUndo === s.canUndo`), `preventExtensions` always false / `isExtensible` always true (so `Object.freeze(handle)` cannot break a proxy invariant), `getPrototypeOf` → null once revoked, and `has`/`ownKeys`/`getOwnPropertyDescriptor` switching to the read-only handle. The new `describe('a disposed editor is inert')` block in editor-read-only.test.ts only asserts that writes no-op and reads still work; the equivalent assertions that exist for `readOnlyDocStore` (e.g. editor-read-only.test.ts:940 `Object.getPrototypeOf(editor.getStore())).not.toBeNull()`) have no disposed-path counterpart, and there is no test importing `revocableDocStore` directly.

samples.summary: The identical `isDisposed()` guard added to `insertImageFromUrl` has no test; only the file path got one
samples.evidence: image-insert.test.ts gained `"inserts nothing when the editor was disposed under the upload"` for `insertImageFromFile`, but the test file never imports or calls `insertImageFromUrl` (its imports at line 6 list only `insertImageFromFile` and `shareTokenImageUploader`). The URL path has the same await-then-write shape (`loadImageDimensions` round trip) and the same guard plus a `return false`, entirely uncovered.

samples.summary: `withUndoUnit`'s documented 'held render replays even after a throw' behaviour is untested
samples.evidence: The doc comment claims interior `requestRender()` calls are replayed once after the outermost unit commits 'including after a throw', implemented via the `finally` block at text-editor.ts:3862-3869. The only render-deferral test (editor-undo-selection.test.ts, 'paints once for the whole action, after the unit commits') covers the success path only. If the replay-on-throw regressed, a failed edit would leave the screen showing pre-edit content indefinitely — user-visible but only on an error path.
searchedFor: grep withUndoUnit|renderAfterUndoUnit in packages/docs/test and packages/frontend/tests
read the new paint-count test in editor-undo-selection.test.ts

samples.summary: `willWrite()` was added to ~30 mutators but redo-clearing is only asserted through `insertText`
samples.evidence: The new memory.test.ts cases ('a batch that writes drops redo history', 'a write after an adopted empty batch still drops redo', etc.) all drive redo invalidation via `insertText`. Nothing pins that the structural/document-level mutators that also gained the call — `setDocument`, `replaceDocument`, `setDocStyles`, `setHeader/setFooter`, the table mutators — clear redo, so dropping `willWrite()` from any of them would go unnoticed.

finding.evidence: This diff adds `readOnly` to the effect deps in three views. `notes-view-readonly.test.tsx` and `slides-view-readonly.test.tsx` are new and pin the rebuild+dispose for notes/slides, but nothing mounts `DocsView`: `grep -l 'DocsView|docs-view' packages/frontend/**/*.test.*` returns only `yorkie-doc-store.test.ts`, `docs-context-menu.test.tsx` and `docs-table-context-menu.test.tsx`, none of which render DocsView or exercise a readOnly flip. A regression that drops `readOnly` from the deps again, or that disposes the store while the editor still needs it, would ship green.

verdict.reason: No test anywhere in the repo mounts DocsView or exercises its readOnly-driven rebuild / store.dispose() cleanup, although notes and slides have dedicated tests for exactly that behavior. docs-view.tsx:359 captures readOnly at initialize(), disposes the store at :574, and lists readOnly in the deps at :590. Repo-wide grep of *.test.*/*.spec.* for DocsView|docs-view yields only yorkie-doc-store.test.ts, docs-context-menu.test.tsx, docs-table-context-menu.test.tsx (none render the view) plus unrelated packages/docs editor tests. I also checked the separate packages/frontend/tests tree (docs-find-bar-read-only.test.tsx only renders DocsFindBar with a mocked editor), indirect mounts via docs-detail/shared-document/revision-preview (revision-preview.tsx:783 reimplements its own initialize call), source-scanning tests (detail-layout-subscriptions.test.ts covers board/notes/slides detail files only), and the absence of any e2e suite. yorkie-doc-store.test.ts has no 'dispose' reference at all. Blocking under the test-adequacy rubric: a changed permission boundary (a downgraded share-link visitor keeping a writable editor) with no meaningful test, so a regression dropping readOnly from the deps ships green.

finding.summary: The share-link periodic revalidation rewrite (useEffect → useQuery with refetchInterval/retry/error handling) has no test at all
finding.evidence: `SharedDocumentByToken` was rewritten from a one-shot `resolveShareLink` effect to a react-query poll (`refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS`, `refetchOnWindowFocus`, `retry: 1`) plus a new missing-token/error branch. Grepping `packages/frontend` `*.test.*` for `shared-document` / `SharedDocumentByToken` / `resolveShareLink` finds only `shared-blob-routing.test.ts`, `user-presence.test.tsx` and `template-review-queue.test.tsx` — none render this component. Untested behaviours that matter: a downgraded role actually propagating to `readOnly`, a revoked link closing the view, and the claimed 'two attempts have to fail before eviction' (a single blip must not evict a working session). Both failure directions are user-visible (a revoked editor keeps writing, or a healthy session is thrown out).

verdict.reason: The rewritten `SharedDocumentByToken` (shared-document.tsx:1090-1140) is a react-query poll (`refetchInterval: SHARE_LINK_REVALIDATE_MS` at :88/:1115, `refetchOnWindowFocus`, `retry: 1`) with a missing-token/error eviction branch (:1121-1137) whose `resolved.role` drives `readOnly` in every shared layout (:190, :331, :384, :434, :461, :749). I searched both frontend test roots (`src/**` and the separate `packages/frontend/tests/**`, 375 files) plus repo-wide greps and found no test that mounts this component: the only two test files touching the module are `shared-blob-routing.test.ts:2`, which imports solely the pure `sharedBlobKind` helper, and `template-review-queue.test.tsx:30-34`, which mocks the entire module out with a stub div. `public-templates.test.tsx:56` renders `<App/>` but stubs the `/t/:id` route. No frontend test references `refetchInterval`, window-focus refetch, or 60s timer advancement, and there is no e2e/playwright suite. So the revalidation cadence, the two-failures-before-eviction claim, and role-downgrade propagation to `readOnly` are entirely untested; both failure directions (revoked editor keeps writing, or a healthy session evicted on one blip) are user-visible, making this a major missing-test gap rather than a contained edge case.

finding.summary: The two new Cmd+Shift+V guard tests are purely negative with no positive control, so they pass vacuously if the shortcut never fires
finding.evidence: Both new tests (`…resolves during the yield is refused`, `…resolves after dispose writes nothing`) only assert that 'PLAIN' is absent from the document. Neither asserts that `readText` was ever called, and `installPendingClipboard` returns no spy handle for that. If `dispatchPastePlain` failed to reach `pastePlainTextFromClipboard` (modifier/platform gating in `handleKeyDown`, or a future refactor of the shortcut), the clipboard read never happens and both tests still pass — i.e. the `this.disposed || this.pasting` guard added at text-editor.ts:4273 would be uncovered while appearing covered. Contrast `editor-read-only.test.ts`'s disposal paste test, which pairs the negative with a 'control: the same paste lands when the editor is still alive' case, and `editor-undo-selection.test.ts`, which asserts `readText` was called.

verdict.reason: The tests are exactly as described: both new Cmd+Shift+V tests assert only absence of 'PLAIN' (large-paste-indicator.test.ts:423-424 and :450), and installPendingClipboard (:137-157) stubs readText as a bare arrow returning a pending promise with no spy handle, so no test can assert the read fired. I checked whether the negative-only shape still discriminates the new guard at text-editor.ts:4273. For the 'during the yield' test it does today: handleKeyDown is bound at text-editor.ts:763, mod is true on either platform (:1088) because the helper sets both ctrlKey and metaKey, case 'v' reaches pastePlainTextFromClipboard at :1373-1376, and only `this.pasting` at :4273 stops the write. So the reviewer's stated mechanism ('shortcut never fires') is hypothetical, not current. But the dispose test is genuinely non-discriminating for the `this.disposed` half of the same new guard: editor.ts:1138-1140 builds the Doc over revocableDocStore(docStore, () => disposed), and read-only.ts:190-204 with :96-117 turn every mutator into a silent no-op once disposed flips (set at editor.ts:4475, before textEditor.dispose() at :4486). A PLAIN write attempted with the :4273 disposed check removed would be swallowed by the revoked store, so store.getDocument() still reads 'seed' and the test passes either way. That is a negative-only test presented as coverage for a newly added guard it cannot fail on, with no positive control anywhere (no other docs test references readText). The reviewer's contrast citations are partly wrong (editor-undo-selection.test.ts does not exist), which weakens the rhetoric but not the substance. No named refutation ground applies: the code is present as quoted, nothing makes the gap unreachable, and fake coverage over a new guard is squarely in this lens.

finding.summary: No test anywhere covers the new `dispose()` → `isDisposed()`/neutered-mutators behavior on a real editor
finding.evidence: The delta's core new behavior lives in `packages/docs/src/view/editor.ts`: `dispose()` now sets `disposed = true` and calls `neuterMutations(api)`, and `isDisposed()` is a new `EditorAPI` member. I grepped the whole repo's test files for `isDisposed`, `neuterMutations` and "disposed" — the only hits are the frontend `image-insert.test.ts` fake (`isDisposed: vi.fn().mockReturnValue(disposed)`), which mocks the very thing under test away. `packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts` exercises the read-only branch of `MUTATING_METHODS` (insertLink/insertTable/applyStyle) but nothing calls `dispose()` and then asserts `editor.isDisposed() === true` or that e.g. `insertTable`/`applyStyle`/`pasteFormat` are inert afterwards. If `dispose()` forgot the flag, forgot the `neuterMutations` call, or the ordering broke, every suite stays green while the stale-holder write this PR exists to block lands silently.

verdict.reason: The finding claims no test anywhere covers `dispose()` → `isDisposed()`/neutered-mutators on a real editor, and specifically that packages/docs/test/view/editor-read-only.test.ts never calls dispose() and asserts on it. That is false. That exact file has a describe block 'a disposed editor is inert' (line 957) that builds a REAL editable editor through the real factory (`initialize` from ../../src/view/editor.js, line 4; mountEditable at 973-993 with readOnly=false over a real MemDocStore) and then: asserts isDisposed() is false before dispose() and true after (995-1000); calls applyStyle/setBlockType/toggleList/insertTable/insertLink/undo after dispose() and asserts the underlying store is unchanged — text still 'hello', one block, still 'paragraph', bold undefined (1002-1021), i.e. real state assertions, not mock-call assertions, so they fail if neuterMutations is missing or ordered after the mutators; asserts pasteFormat() returns false rather than undefined after disposal (1025-1029); asserts stale and fresh getStore()/getDoc() handles stop writing but keep reading (1034-1056); and includes a control test proving the same handles DO write before disposal (1058-1064), which rules out the tests passing vacuously. There is also a test that an in-flight paste() resuming after disposal writes nothing (1093+). A plain grep for `isDisposed` returns hits at lines 995/997/999 of this file, contradicting the finding's stated search result that only the frontend mock matched.
